title: Core block set, version 1
description: The standard block types every template may use (Q64). Each `$defs` entry named after a block type is that block's shape; `packages/core/render/blocks.tsx` maps each to core components. `settings.{Layout}` entries are the options of core layout components. Every word a person reads, including labels and messages, is in the block (Q64); words are plain text (backticks for inline code are the only mark); pictures are asset ids; `/layout` links point at a layout of the same template.

sectionTitleSize.description: The section title at the top steps of the type ramp (MP16), for a brand page's section and closing titles: `display` or `jumbo`. Without it the title is the usual section size; the heading level still follows the outline.

text.description: Words a person reads: a non-empty string, or a value not yet confirmed (DP4).

words.description: Words that may be empty: a string, or a value not yet confirmed (DP4).

unconfirmed.description: A value not yet confirmed (DP4): { "unconfirmed": "speaker" }. The renderer shows the template's phrase for the key (the shared file's `strings.unconfirmed`, such as "Speaker to confirm"); the content check counts them by file and `--release` fails on any.

richText.description: Rich inline text (DP1): a plain string, or a list of strings and marked runs ({ "text", "mark" }). Marks: emphasis, strong, accent (the brand colour, Text tone accent), code, link (with href) and break (a new line, { "mark": "break" }). No markup.

richHeading.description: Rich inline text for a title (DP1): a plain string, or a list of strings and runs marked emphasis, accent or break. No markup.

asset.description: A picture's id in the template's assets.json.

action.description: A button in a block. It goes somewhere (`href`: a layout as "/layout", an anchor as "#id", or an address) or, in an example that leads nowhere yet, says something when pressed (`says`). At least one; with both, it goes.

primary.description: The main action: one per part at most.

href.description: Where it goes: "/layout" for a layout of this template (checked), "#id" for a heading on the page, or an address. Drawn as a link that looks like a button.

says.description: What the page says when the action is pressed, while it leads nowhere in an example: "Quotes aren’t part of this example."

current.description: The layout id marked current in the header.

width.description: The main column: wide (default) or a reading column.

opening.description: Spaced (default): the page's space above the first band; flush: the first band meets the header, for an opening picture or tinted band.

state.description: A state layout's screen state (Q65 TP2–TP3). A state file with only settings inherits its screen's regions; blocks that know the state draw it in their own box: a form `failed` or `done`, a list `empty`.

site-header.description: A site's header: name, mark, the places (layouts) and actions.

site-footer.description: A site's footer: titled link sections and the small print.

hero.description: An opening: eyebrow, title, lead, actions, a note and a picture.

standalone.description: A statement meant to be read on its own (a brand opening): the page presents it framed. Leave it out on task and reference pages, whose title and intro sit with their content (Q91).

media.description: Slot hero.media (DP11): blocks in the picture's place when there's no picture. Takes gallery, or a template's own block.

decoration.description: Decoration over the opening's picture (MP9, LR20): the name of one of the template's decoration presets (shapes, marks), hidden from screen readers. Only with a picture.

reserve.description: Lines of room kept for the title and the lead (MP7), so a series of pages (a project's, a year's) keeps one opening height. Longer text still grows the opening.

stats.description: Figures in a grid under a heading.

cards.description: Cards in a grid under a heading.

empty.description: The list with nothing in it (Q65 TP3): why it is empty and what to do, drawn in the list's own box in the screen state `empty`.

points.description: A bulleted list under a heading.

details.description: Terms and their details under a heading.

form.description: A form that sends once, then says what happens next.

answer.description: The failed screen state's kept answer: shown in the field when the form failed; required fields without one are marked at fault.

invalid.description: With answer: the words under the field when that kept answer is the fault.

choose.description: The prompt in an empty choice: "Choose one".

enter.description: The message for an empty required text field; {field} is its label in lower case: "Enter {field}."

pick.description: The message for an empty required choice: "Choose {field}."

links.description: Links under the button: another way through the flow ("Forgot your password?", "Create an account").

error.description: Why a send was refused and how to fix it: revealed above the fields, which keep their values, in the screen state `failed` (Q65 TP2).

outcome.description: What the form becomes in its own box once it is sent (Q65 TP2): shown in place of the form, through Morph, and as the screen state `done`. Without it, a confirmation takes the button's place.

cta.description: A closing call to action: the words and the actions side by side.

standalone.description: A closing invitation meant to stand on its own (a marketing or editorial page's last word): the page frames it. Leave it out on task pages (Q91).

illustration.description: Drawn art from the template's assets (MP22): an asset marked `illustration` drawn inline by Illustration, its colours from tokens in every scheme, its size groups by its own width, its motion as the asset's `play` says. Its `alt` names it; a decorative asset is skipped by screen readers.

ratio.description: The frame, over the asset's own ratio; `natural` takes the drawing's viewBox.

breadcrumbs.description: Where the page sits: home, each level, the page itself last without a link.

byline.description: Who wrote it and when, under an article's title; `picture` names the author's portrait in assets.json.

person.description: A person, large: name, role and a few lines; `picture` names their portrait in assets.json, `portrait` alone shows their initials.

prose.description: An article's body as structured items: no markup.

decoration.description: Decoration over the picture (MP9, LR20): the name of one of the template's decoration presets (shapes, marks), hidden from screen readers.

posts.description: A list of posts, newest first, each a row card, with paging.

pagingLabel.description: Names the paging: "Older articles". Required with more than one page.

empty.description: The list with nothing in it (Q65 TP3): why it is empty and what to do, drawn in the list's own box in the screen state `empty`.

people.description: People as a grid of portraits with name and role; each item's `picture` names its portrait in assets.json (initials when there's none).

schedule.description: A programme over one or more days: a tab per day, each an agenda.

empty.description: The list with nothing in it (Q65 TP3): why it is empty and what to do, drawn in the list's own box in the screen state `empty`.

tickets.description: Choose a ticket and how many; the total follows; then a hold is confirmed in place.

questions.description: Common questions, each opened on its own.

decoration.description: A decoration preset by name (LR20): the template registers its decorations (registry.decorations) and a block names one; art is the template's, the block stays a fixed configuration. The older form, a list of the template's own blocks, is deprecated and still drawn.

slot.description: Blocks a block holds (DP11 named slots). Each is a block by its type; which types a slot takes is listed with the slot, and a template's own (namespaced) block types are taken in every slot.

split.description: Deprecated (LR18, composition rule: no page inside a block): put blocks side by side with the page's `grid` instead. Kept so existing pages render unchanged. Two columns of blocks side by side, stacking when narrow: slots split.start and split.end. Each takes content blocks (prose, points, details, quote, stats, cards, gallery, people, questions, agenda, schedule, posts, person, byline, alert, empty, form, search, settings, tickets) or a template's own.

ratio.description: The columns' shares (Grid ratio); equal without it.

grid.description: Deprecated (LR18, composition rule: no page inside a block): put blocks side by side with the page's `grid` instead. Kept so existing pages render unchanged. Blocks in equal columns: slot grid.items, taking the same content blocks as split.

items: Step-free entrance on the side street

alert.description: A message about the screen or a part of it: what happened and what to do, in its tone. Errors that block the person, a warning before something lasting, a success that needs no page of its own.

examples.title: Your changes aren’t saved yet
examples.text: Save before you leave this page, or they’ll be lost.

status.description: A whole page that says where the person is when the screen they wanted can't be shown: not found, an error on our side, down for maintenance, sold out, sent. A code or eyebrow, a title, why, and the ways on.

eyebrow.description: A short label above the title: "Error 404", "Order 4417".

empty.description: A list, search or place with nothing in it yet: why it's empty and what to do, in the content's own place.

examples.title: No saved items yet
examples.text: Save something you want to come back to and it appears here.

search.description: Search results with their query: the person can change the words and the list narrows to the results that match; when none do, an empty state says why and what to try.

label.description: The search field's label: "Search the site".

summary.description: Above the results; {count} and {query} are filled in: "{count} results for “{query}”".

none.description: What shows when nothing matches; {query} is filled in.

settings.description: Settings in named groups: on/off settings as switches and one-of-several settings as choices, each saved as soon as it changes (one confirmation per change).

saved.description: Said after each change; {setting} is its label: "{setting} saved."

on.description: A switch: on to start with.

value.description: A choice: the option chosen to start with.
